requirements.title: Client Registry is issuing authority
requirements.statement: Client Registry SHALL be the only service that creates or assigns the canonical Symphonix Patient Identifier.
requirements.source: Architecture review of BulletTrain client_registry and shared_health_record
acceptance_criteria: No patient-data service creates PAT-* or UUID clinical patient identifiers when a patient is missing.
All new patient creation flows call Client Registry or consume a registry-issued creation event.

requirements.title: NHS-style checksum shape
requirements.statement: SPID SHALL be exactly 10 digits and SHALL pass the modulus-11 check digit algorithm used by the UK NHS number format.
requirements.source: NHS Data Dictionary NHS NUMBER format
acceptance_criteria: Spaces and hyphens are accepted at API boundaries.
The stored canonical form is 10 digits.
Invalid modulus-11 values are rejected.

requirements.title: Not an NHS number
requirements.statement: SPID SHALL NOT be labelled, stored, emitted, or documented as an NHS Number.
requirements.source: User architecture directive; NHS Number is an external identifier only
acceptance_criteria: FHIR identifier system for SPID is Symphonix-owned.
Real NHS Number, if present, remains an external alias with the NHS Number system.
Internal API fields use patient_id, spid, or symphonix_patient_id, not nhs_number.

requirements.title: FHIR Patient identity binding
requirements.statement: FHIR Patient.id and Patient.identifier SHALL include the SPID for every patient-data exchange.
acceptance_criteria: Patient.id equals SPID unless a FHIR facade must preserve an external logical id.
Patient.identifier includes the Symphonix patient identifier system.
Patient references use Patient/{SPID}.

requirements.title: Canonical envelope carries patient identity
requirements.statement: Bridge envelopes and agent messages carrying patient data SHALL expose the canonical SPID as structured metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Patient-data envelopes include patient_id with a valid SPID.
Envelopes include identifier_system and identity_version when available.
Patient identity metadata is available to adapters without parsing free text.

requirements.title: Creation event propagation
requirements.statement: Client Registry SHALL publish a patient.identity.created event for every committed patient creation.
acceptance_criteria: The event is written through an outbox in the same transaction as patient creation.
The event includes SPID, identity version, correlation id, idempotency key, demographics hash, and lifecycle status.
Shared HealthRecord and patient-data siblings upsert their local patient projection from the event.

requirements.title: Subscriber projection contract
requirements.statement: Every patient-data service SHALL maintain a local patient context keyed by SPID and reconciled from identity events.
acceptance_criteria: Projection upserts are idempotent.
Local domain records reference SPID but retain local encounter/order/episode identifiers.
Projection version regressions are rejected or ignored.

requirements.title: Reject unknown or inactive patient writes
requirements.statement: Patient-data services SHALL reject non-emergency clinical writes when SPID is unknown, invalid, inactive, confused, restricted without permitted purpose, or deceased.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown patient writes fail closed with a typed patient_identity error.
Emergency writes require break-glass metadata and audit.
Blocked writes emit operational telemetry.

requirements.title: Idempotent outbox delivery
requirements.statement: Identity events SHALL use idempotency keys and replayable outbox semantics across EventBus, hub, Nexus A2A, and subscriber adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate events do not create duplicate patient projections.
Dead-lettered events are replayable after correction.
Reconciliation can prove registry and subscriber identity versions match.

requirements.title: Confused record workflow
requirements.statement: Potential confused records SHALL be placed under review and resolved by an NBO-style human approval workflow before merge, split, or reassignment.
requirements.source: NHS PDS National Back Office data quality guidance
acceptance_criteria: Automated matching can recommend but cannot complete a confused-record correction.
Affected records are flagged as under_review/confused.
Outbound notifications and non-essential automated agent actions are suppressed until resolved.

requirements.title: Merge and link audit
requirements.statement: Confirmed duplicates SHALL be merged or linked with alias retention, event replay, and immutable audit history.
requirements.source: NHS duplicate NHS Number handling pattern
acceptance_criteria: Old identifiers remain aliases and cannot be reissued.
All subscribers receive merge/link events.
A full audit trail records approver, source evidence, and affected resources.

requirements.title: Stop-note and sensitive status
requirements.statement: Restricted access, historically described as stop-noting, SHALL be represented as a sensitive/restricted identity state and propagated to services.
requirements.source: NHS PDS access restriction and S-flag guidance
acceptance_criteria: Location/contact details are withheld from services without an allowed purpose.
Automated agent reads and notifications are suppressed unless policy allows.
Break-glass reads are audited and visible in patient safety telemetry.

requirements.title: Death status propagation
requirements.statement: Formal and informal death status SHALL be modelled, audited, and propagated without deleting the patient record.
requirements.source: NHS Notify death-status handling and NHS records-management retention guidance
acceptance_criteria: Active care loops, appointments, recalls, and notifications are stopped or routed to permitted administrative workflows.
The clinical record remains retained according to policy.
Incorrect death status can be corrected through an audited reinstatement event.

requirements.title: Identity lifecycle audit
requirements.statement: Every identity lifecycle transition SHALL emit an immutable audit record with actor, system, reason, correlation id, and before/after state.
requirements.source: PDS audit expectations and Symphonix observability baseline
acceptance_criteria: Audit spans registry, hub, agent, and subscriber processing.
Audit records are queryable by SPID and correlation id.
Manual approvals include approver role and evidence references.

requirements.title: Agent recommendations require deterministic guardrails
requirements.statement: Agents MAY detect, reconcile, and recommend patient identity fixes, but SHALL NOT autonomously create identifiers, merge records, remove restrictions, or change death status.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic services own ID generation, validation, and state transitions.
Agent proposals are evidence-bearing tasks requiring human approval for high-risk changes.
Guardrails prevent privileged identity mutation through prompt/tool paths.

requirements.title: Closed-loop reconciliation
requirements.statement: A scheduled closed-loop reconciliation SHALL compare Client Registry with all patient-data projections and open remediation tasks for drift.
acceptance_criteria: Drift reports include missing patients, stale versions, invalid identifiers, and lifecycle mismatches.
Reconciliation uses deterministic checks before agent triage.
Resolved drift replays missing events or applies approved corrective events.

requirements.title: Minimum disclosure
requirements.statement: Patient identity propagation SHALL disclose only fields needed by each subscriber purpose and SHALL carry consent and purpose-of-use metadata.
requirements.source: PDS access restriction model and Symphonix PHI controls
acceptance_criteria: Subscribers receive pseudonymized or hashed demographics where full demographics are not needed.
Purpose-of-use is enforced at registry, hub, and subscriber boundaries.
Restricted records suppress contact/location data by default.

requirements.title: Migration without patient-record loss
requirements.statement: Migration from mpiId, nationalID, nhs_number, and local PAT-* identifiers SHALL preserve aliases and map every patient-data record to exactly one active SPID or one explicit under-review exception.
acceptance_criteria: Every migrated identifier has a reversible alias mapping or an under-review case.
No clinical resource is dropped during migration.
Backfill reports are signed off before write-path enforcement is enabled.
